We remember January 2016 as an echo of one calendar event. Eighty-four of us said "state of the union," and seventy-nine of us said "state of the union address," both peaking on 2016-01-12. Forty-eight of us reached for "final state of the," forty-seven for "final state of the union," and forty-six for "final state of the union address" — each first said among us by R000586 on 2016-01-05, each peaking the same day, the twelfth.

Before the address, on 2016-01-05, another current moved through us: thirty-nine said "reduce gun violence," thirty-two said "to reduce gun violence," and thirty-six said "executive actions to." The phrase "reduce gun violence" was first said by P000593, back on 2013-01-04.

That is the record of us this era: one scheduled speech, one week of executive action on guns, and our numbers converging on the same few words.
